title: Evolving a Running Architecture Without a Big-Bang Rewrite
objective: Plan a three-step evolution of a prior decision that names what is dual-running in each step, the compatibility contract during overlap, and the last reversible step.
whyThisMatters: The architecture you can defend on day one is not the architecture you will be asked to live with in year three. The skill is not picking a better style — it is getting from here to there without a rewrite that has no rollback. Compatibility during overlap is the decision; the target style is just the destination.
evidence: A migration sequence of at least three steps that names, for each step, what is dual-running and which clients or writers have moved
An ADR stating the compatibility contract (API, event schema, or data representation) that must hold for the whole overlap, and marking the prior target-style ADR as still in force or superseded
A rollback note naming the last step that is still reversible and the inspectable evidence that would trigger rollback
acceptanceCriteria: The sequence has at least three steps, and each step names what is dual-running (two writers, two read paths, or old and new event consumers).
The ADR states a compatibility contract that must hold for the overlap and names at least one change that is forbidden during that overlap.
The rollback note names the last reversible step by number and names the evidence (a metric, an error budget, a failed contract test) that would trigger rollback.
